notable_features.text: Icelandic is a North Germanic language closely related to Faroese and western Norwegian dialects, though not mutually intelligible with the continental Scandinavian languages. It has a relatively large phoneme inventory of 45 sounds and a rich tense/aspect system marking 5 WALS categories, while maintaining basic SVO word order. Despite being closely related in written form to Faroese, the two languages' spoken forms are not mutually intelligible with each other.
